READ: nothing further; built on the stage record above.
OBSERVED: answer below.

TITLE: Behaviour-warped Poincare metric inside residual-quantizer assignment and reconstruction

COST: Marginal per-step cost is one d x r projection per (item, code) pair inside the assignment loop, negligible versus the encoder: at the frozen scale, ~1023 items per step (24556 items / 24 steps), 3 levels, K=256 codes per level, d=64, r=8 gives 1023*3*256*(64+8*64) ~ 0.5 GFLOP per step, on the order of 5-8 percent of one step's encoder+decoder work, so ~5-8 percent wall-clock over 72,000 steps (3000 epochs x 24). One-off precompute: sparse PPMI over the training transition graph, 24556 items, truncated SVD rank 16, then a rank-r eigendecomposition of a 16x16 successor covariance per item; minutes on CPU, done once before Stage 2 and frozen. No extra backward pass (V_i is detached).
HYPOTHESIS: If behaviour anisotropy is aligned with the latent directions along which next-item identity varies, the quantizer will spend its finite codebook on those directions, items that share a successor profile will share more prefix tokens, the conditional entropy H(sid_2 | sid_1) and H(sid_3 | sid_1,sid_2) will drop, and Stage 3 test recall@10 will move from the baseline band to above 0.065 in the single frozen run. Observable in one run as: higher measured successor-prefix agreement and higher Stage 3 test_recall@10 than the recorded baseline.

The +rho sign (extra distance, hence extra resolution, along behaviour-varying directions) is argued from rate allocation and could be backwards for this data. Items with concentrated successors (rho near 1 on one direction) may over-fragment prefixes for popular items. Bounded 2x dynamic range of the loss could mildly interact with the learning rate.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Directed item transitions from training sequences only, summarised per item as its successor distribution and the successor covariance directions.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From the training split only: build the directed count matrix N[i,j] over consecutive pairs in training sequences (25,456 training items). Row-normalise with add-alpha smoothing, alpha = 1/V (documented default), to get P(j|i). Build PPMI: pmi = log( P(j|i) / P_col(j) ), PPMI = max(pmi, 0), then truncated SVD rank 16 giving y_i in R^16, each y_i normalised to unit L2. For item i take its top-8 successors by P(j|i) (fewer if the item has fewer), compute the weighted centroid c_i = sum_j p_j y_j and deviations e_j = y_j - c_i; set Vhat_i = [sqrt(p_1) e_1, ..., sqrt(p_8) e_8] in R^{16x8}. HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Inside quantization: in the assignment distance that picks mu_{l,k} at every residual level l = 1..L, and in the reconstruction/commitment term that scores the final prefix point against the item. It therefore acts on the whole prefix hierarchy, not on one level.
COUPLING PATH: item -> frozen PPMI successor covariance Vhat_i (behaviour) -> learned alignment W -> per-item basis V_i -> trace-normalised anisotropy rho_i(p, mu) computed on the tangent residual log_p(mu) -> warped distance D_i -> argmin over the level codebook AND the reconstruction term -> chosen code sequence (k_1..k_L) -> Stage 2 parameter updates and, downstream, the SID vocabulary consumed by Stage 3. COUPLING EQUATION: D_i(p, mu)^2 = d_Poincare(p, mu; c=1)^2 * ( 1 + ||V_i^T log_p(mu)||^2 / ((tr(V_i V_i^T) + eps) * ||log_p(mu)||^2 + eps) ), with V_i = W Vhat_i, W in R^{64x16} trainable, Vhat_i frozen training-only successor covariance.
OBSERVABLES: (a) assignment: the per-level histogram of chosen codes for behaviourally diverse items shifts toward codes whose tangent offsets align with V_i, and the measured successor-prefix agreement (fraction of consecutive training pairs whose SIDs share >= 1 and >= 2 leading tokens) rises; (b) gradient/parameter: codebook points move along behaviour-varying directions, visible as an increase in the projection of codebook displacement onto the span of W; (c) predictability: H(sid_2|sid_1) and H(sid_3|sid_1,sid_2) drop on held-out training sequences; (d) Stage 3 test recall@10 in the single frozen run.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: phi_behavior = 0, i.e. V_i := 0 for every item, so rho_i := 0 and D_i^2 = d_P^2 exactly; the code then runs the unmodified hyperbolic RQ assignment and reconstruction with the identical codebook size, schedule and loss weights.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: curvature set so that the base term is Euclidean, i.e. d_P^2 replaced by ||p - mu||^2 and log_p(mu) replaced by (mu - p), while V_i and rho_i are unchanged, giving a flat Mahalanobis-warped RQ.
ABLATION BOTH ON: the full run: c = 1 Poincare base term and V_i from the frozen training-only successor covariance, both active in the same argmin and the same reconstruction term.   # one-off, training split only, frozen
  P[j|i] = (N[i,j] + 1/V) / (sum_j' N[i,j'] + 1)
  PPMI[i,j] = max(0, log( P[j|i] / (sum_i' N[i',j] / sum_{i',j'} N[i',j']) ))
  Y = svd_trunc(PPMI, rank=16);  y_i = Y[i] / (||Y[i]|| + 1e-12)
  top8(i) = argsort_j P[j|i] desc, first min(8, nnz_i)

  Vhat_i = concat_j [ sqrt(P[j|i]) * (y_j - c_i) ]   # 16 x min(8,nnz_i), zeros if nnz_i = 0
  # per step
  x = encoder(item)                      # in ball, ||x|| <= (1 - 1e-3)/sqrt(c)
  p = x; loss = 0
  for l in 1..L:
      for k in 1..K:
          u = log_p(mu[l,k])                              # tangent at p
          dP2 = poincare_dist2(p, mu[l,k], c)
          rho = ||V_i^T u||^2 / ((trace(V_i V_i^T) + 1e-8) * ||u||^2 + 1e-8)
          rho = clamp(rho, 0.0, 1.0)
          D2[l,k] = dP2 * (1.0 + rho)
      k* = argmin_k D2[l,k]
      u = log_p(mu[l,k*])
      r = log_p(x)                                         # tangent residual at p
      loss += lambda_l * D2[l,k*]                          # warped reconstruction of this level
      p = exp_p(r - u)                                     # hyperbolic RQ residual update
      commit += ||r - u||^2
  loss += beta * commit
  # switches: phi_behavior=0 -> V_i := 0 ; phi_geometry=0 -> dP2 := ||p-mu||^2, log/exp := identity affine
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: the item's encoder point x in the curvature-1 Poincare ball, the level codebooks mu[l,1..K] in the ball, and the frozen per-item successor covariance Vhat_i (plus trainable W). Outputs: the discrete SID (k_1..k_L), the warped per-level reconstruction loss and the commitment term, and the gradient with respect to encoder parameters, codebooks and W.
SAFEGUARDS: clamp every point to radius (1 - 1e-3)/sqrt(c) before log/exp; add 1e-8 inside every ||.||^2 denominator; clamp rho into [0,1] (it is bounded analytically by Cauchy-Schwarz, the clamp only absorbs float error); set V_i := 0 whenever the item has fewer than 2 distinct successors or its covariance trace is < 1e-8, which makes that item's assignment exactly plain Poincare; declare D2 inf for codes that would produce a non-finite log map; keep c fixed at 1 so the conformal factor 1/(1-c||x||^2) never blows up; detach Vhat_i and normalise every y_i to unit norm so the warp is invariant to the arbitrary scale of the PPMI SVD.
END IDEA`;

NOVELTY: The earlier mechanisms relocate or reweight codebook points (successor-Frechet centroids, radial placement from context entropy, per-level curvature, successor geodesic shift, cone constraints, Lorentz profile smoothing). BEHMET-RQ leaves the codebook points and their update rule untouched and instead makes the DISTANCE ITSELF behaviour-anisotropic: a per-item, trace-normalised covariance of the item's successor directions is inserted multiplicatively into the Poincare distance used for assignment and reconstruction, so the curved metric allocates finer effective resolution along the directions in which that item's behaviour varies. The warp is bounded in [1,2] by construction, so no coupling weight exists to tune.
CHANGE: Each training item gets a frozen, training-only successor-covariance basis V_i (rank r, trace-normalised so the anisotropy budget is exactly one Euclidean dimension); the residual-quantizer assignment and its reconstruction term use D_i^2 = d_Poincare^2 * (1 + rho_i) with rho_i in [0,1] the normalised alignment of the tangent residual with V_i.
SPECIFICATION: See SPEC EQUATIONS; encoder output x_i in the Poincare ball of curvature c=1; at each RQ level l the query point is the running prefix point p_{l-1}; the chosen code is argmin_k D_i(p_{l-1}, mu_{l,k})^2; the residual is carried by log/exp maps at p_{l-1}; loss = sum_l lambda_l * D_i(p_l, x_i)^2 + beta * commitment, with lambda_l and beta unchanged from the baseline RQ-VAE (they are not part of this mechanism).
COST: Marginal per-step cost is one d x r projection per (item, code) pair inside the assignment loop, negligible versus the encoder: at the frozen scale, ~1023 items per step (24556 items / 24 steps), 3 levels, K=256 codes per level, d=64, r=8 gives 1023*3*256*(64+8*64) ~ 0.5 GFLOP per step, on the order of 5-8 percent of one step's encoder+decoder work, so ~5-8 percent wall-clock over 72,000 steps (3000 epochs x 24). One-off precompute: sparse PPMI over the training transition graph, 24556 items, truncated SVD rank 16, then a rank-r eigendecomposition of a 16x16 successor covariance per item; minutes on CPU, done once before Stage 2 and frozen. No extra backward pass (V_i is detached).
HYPOTHESIS: If behaviour anisotropy is aligned with the latent directions along which next-item identity varies, the quantizer will spend its finite codebook on those directions, items that share a successor profile will share more prefix tokens, the conditional entropy H(sid_2 | sid_1) and H(sid_3 | sid_1,sid_2) will drop, and Stage 3 test recall@10 will move from the baseline band to above 0.065 in the single frozen run. Observable in one run as: higher measured successor-prefix agreement and higher Stage 3 test_recall@10 than the recorded baseline.
RISKS: The PPMI successor basis may be only weakly related to the latent space, in which case the learned alignment W degenerates to an arbitrary rotation and the warp becomes near-isotropic noise in the assignment, leaving recall flat. The +rho sign (extra distance, hence extra resolution, along behaviour-varying directions) is argued from rate allocation and could be backwards for this data. Items with concentrated successors (rho near 1 on one direction) may over-fragment prefixes for popular items. Bounded 2x dynamic range of the loss could mildly interact with the learning rate.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Directed item transitions from training sequences only, summarised per item as its successor distribution and the successor covariance directions.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From the training split only: build the directed count matrix N[i,j] over consecutive pairs in training sequences (25,456 training items). Row-normalise with add-alpha smoothing, alpha = 1/V (documented default), to get P(j|i). Build PPMI: pmi = log( P(j|i) / P_col(j) ), PPMI = max(pmi, 0), then truncated SVD rank 16 giving y_i in R^16, each y_i normalised to unit L2. For item i take its top-8 successors by P(j|i) (fewer if the item has fewer), compute the weighted centroid c_i = sum_j p_j y_j and deviations e_j = y_j - c_i; set Vhat_i = [sqrt(p_1) e_1, ..., sqrt(p_8) e_8] in R^{16x8}. This table is built once from the training split and frozen.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: The transition counts, the PPMI SVD and the per-item covariance all read only training-split sequences; validation and test sequences are never touched, so no validation/test interaction can enter the frozen V_i. The SID codebook sees V_i only through the training quantizer loss, and the Stage 3 evaluator never feeds behaviour back into SID construction. Items whose only evidence is a validation or test occurrence keep the smoothed behaviour table entry, which is computed without them.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Fixed negative curvature c = 1 (ball radius 1), Poincare distance d_P(x,y) = arcosh(1 + 2c||x-y||^2 / ((1-c||x||^2)(1-c||y||^2))), and the Mobius log/exp maps log_p and exp_p used for the residual chain; the metric is warped by the behaviour term, D_i^2 = d_P^2 * (1 + rho_i).
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Inside quantization: in the assignment distance that picks mu_{l,k} at every residual level l = 1..L, and in the reconstruction/commitment term that scores the final prefix point against the item. It therefore acts on the whole prefix hierarchy, not on one level.
COUPLING PATH: item -> frozen PPMI successor covariance Vhat_i (behaviour) -> learned alignment W -> per-item basis V_i -> trace-normalised anisotropy rho_i(p, mu) computed on the tangent residual log_p(mu) -> warped distance D_i -> argmin over the level codebook AND the reconstruction term -> chosen code sequence (k_1..k_L) -> Stage 2 parameter updates and, downstream, the SID vocabulary consumed by Stage 3. Removing the behaviour (V_i = 0) collapses rho_i to 0 and the argmin and loss become exactly plain Poincare RQ; removing the curvature (Euclidean limit) keeps the same rho_i but on flat distances, so the chosen codes and gradients both change. Neither switch can be removed without changing the core computation.
COUPLING EQUATION: D_i(p, mu)^2 = d_Poincare(p, mu; c=1)^2 * ( 1 + ||V_i^T log_p(mu)||^2 / ((tr(V_i V_i^T) + eps) * ||log_p(mu)||^2 + eps) ), with V_i = W Vhat_i, W in R^{64x16} trainable, Vhat_i frozen training-only successor covariance.
OBSERVABLES: (a) assignment: the per-level histogram of chosen codes for behaviourally diverse items shifts toward codes whose tangent offsets align with V_i, and the measured successor-prefix agreement (fraction of consecutive training pairs whose SIDs share >= 1 and >= 2 leading tokens) rises; (b) gradient/parameter: codebook points move along behaviour-varying directions, visible as an increase in the projection of codebook displacement onto the span of W; (c) predictability: H(sid_2|sid_1) and H(sid_3|sid_1,sid_2) drop on held-out training sequences; (d) Stage 3 test recall@10 in the single frozen run.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: phi_behavior = 0, i.e. V_i := 0 for every item, so rho_i := 0 and D_i^2 = d_P^2 exactly; the code then runs the unmodified hyperbolic RQ assignment and reconstruction with the identical codebook size, schedule and loss weights.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: curvature set so that the base term is Euclidean, i.e. d_P^2 replaced by ||p - mu||^2 and log_p(mu) replaced by (mu - p), while V_i and rho_i are unchanged, giving a flat Mahalanobis-warped RQ.
ABLATION BOTH ON: the full run: c = 1 Poincare base term and V_i from the frozen training-only successor covariance, both active in the same argmin and the same reconstruction term. One training run only; the two switched-off configurations exist in code as flags and are validated for correctness on a forward pass, but are not trained.
SPEC EQUATIONS:
  # one-off, training split only, frozen
  P[j|i] = (N[i,j] + 1/V) / (sum_j' N[i,j'] + 1)
  PPMI[i,j] = max(0, log( P[j|i] / (sum_i' N[i',j] / sum_{i',j'} N[i',j']) ))
  Y = svd_trunc(PPMI, rank=16);  y_i = Y[i] / (||Y[i]|| + 1e-12)
  top8(i) = argsort_j P[j|i] desc, first min(8, nnz_i)
  c_i = sum_{j in top8(i)} P[j|i] y_j / sum_{j in top8(i)} P[j|i]
  Vhat_i = concat_j [ sqrt(P[j|i]) * (y_j - c_i) ]   # 16 x min(8,nnz_i), zeros if nnz_i = 0
  # per step
  x = encoder(item)                      # in ball, ||x|| <= (1 - 1e-3)/sqrt(c)
  p = x; loss = 0
  for l in 1..L:
      for k in 1..K:
          u = log_p(mu[l,k])                              # tangent at p
          dP2 = poincare_dist2(p, mu[l,k], c)
          rho = ||V_i^T u||^2 / ((trace(V_i V_i^T) + 1e-8) * ||u||^2 + 1e-8)
          rho = clamp(rho, 0.0, 1.0)
          D2[l,k] = dP2 * (1.0 + rho)
      k* = argmin_k D2[l,k]
      u = log_p(mu[l,k*])
      r = log_p(x)                                         # tangent residual at p
      loss += lambda_l * D2[l,k*]                          # warped reconstruction of this level
      p = exp_p(r - u)                                     # hyperbolic RQ residual update
      commit += ||r - u||^2
  loss += beta * commit
  # switches: phi_behavior=0 -> V_i := 0 ; phi_geometry=0 -> dP2 := ||p-mu||^2, log/exp := identity affine
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: the item's encoder point x in the curvature-1 Poincare ball, the level codebooks mu[l,1..K] in the ball, and the frozen per-item successor covariance Vhat_i (plus trainable W). Outputs: the discrete SID (k_1..k_L), the warped per-level reconstruction loss and the commitment term, and the gradient with respect to encoder parameters, codebooks and W.
SAFEGUARDS: clamp every point to radius (1 - 1e-3)/sqrt(c) before log/exp; add 1e-8 inside every ||.||^2 denominator; clamp rho into [0,1] (it is bounded analytically by Cauchy-Schwarz, the clamp only absorbs float error); set V_i := 0 whenever the item has fewer than 2 distinct successors or its covariance trace is < 1e-8, which makes that item's assignment exactly plain Poincare; declare D2 inf for codes that would produce a non-finite log map; keep c fixed at 1 so the conformal factor 1/(1-c||x||^2) never blows up; detach Vhat_i and normalise every y_i to unit norm so the warp is invariant to the arbitrary scale of the PPMI SVD.
END IDEA`;

await tools.progress.append_progress({content: rec1});

return "ok";"}
